blockers.title: The output law silently narrows file 01's expressly-closed responsibility boundary, without citing it, scoping itself, or recording a design delta
blockers.finding: DR-133's subject is the component-output boundary, and that boundary is already stated in accepted architecture: file 01 §'Closed structural responsibility boundary' at digest 40ab9a3e — the exact digest at which DR-201's adversarial re-review was ACCEPTED — which ends 'The boundary is closed for the distribution transition. A process or library split cannot transfer authority.' Its 'Component may return' column admits declared requirements; capability negotiation input; candidates and provenance; candidate domain result; findings/scores/intermediates; typed faults/cancellation detail; and candidate artifacts and mechanical commitments. The artifact's law admits exactly two outputs, semanticFact and coverage, and places 'finding' in the forbidden list whose presence triggers payload refusal. On file 01's terms a component MAY return candidate findings and the host owns ADMISSION; on the artifact's terms a component that returns a candidate finding has its payload refused. The same divergence applies to typed faults/cancellation detail, declared requirements, capability negotiation input, and candidate artifacts, none of which the artifact admits. Measured: the artifact contains zero occurrences of 'file 01', '01-semantic', 'boundary', 'typed fault', 'cancellation', 'declared requirements' or 'capability negotiation'. It also contains zero occurrences of 'preview', so it cannot be read on its face as a preview-scoped narrowing of the general boundary. A corroborating symptom sits inside the artifact: hostOwned retains 'admissionOfFindings' while the law forbids components from emitting findings at all, so a host-side admission verb is preserved with no candidate source. The narrowing may well be intended and lawful for the preview TypeScript role — D-002 selects a provider-only TypeScript slice — but v1-slice §8 is explicit that where this kind of document and a binding artifact appear inconsistent, the correct act is to stop and record a design delta rather than choose whichever reading is easier. Nothing here records one.
blockers.whyBlocking: The artifact's entire subject is a boundary that accepted architecture already closes. Accepting a contract that redraws that boundary in silence would leave two live and differing statements of the same law, with no recorded delta saying which governs for which role — the exact condition file 01's 'closed' clause exists to prevent, and the condition DR-201's acceptance rests on.
blockers.repair: Cite file 01 §'Closed structural responsibility boundary' at 40ab9a3e as a governing source, then do one of two things explicitly. Either (a) scope the law: state that for the D-002 preview TypeScript role the admitted component outputs are narrowed to facts and Coverage, name each file-01 'may return' entry the narrowing removes, and record the delta with its rationale; or (b) align the law with file 01: admit candidate findings as candidates while keeping admission host-only, and re-express OBL-3's refusal as refusal of component-ADMITTED findings rather than of component-emitted candidates. Either way, reconcile hostOwned.admissionOfFindings with whichever choice is made.

blockers.title: The refusal rule is not total: it keys on the forbidden enumeration rather than on the allowed list, and the enumeration omits three acts file 01 expressly forbids
blockers.finding: outputLaw.refusal.rule reads: 'If a TypeScript component payload contains any forbidden output, the host discards the uncommitted candidates and records a typed non-success.' The trigger is membership in the eight-item forbidden enumeration, not absence from the two-item allowed list. An output that is neither allowed nor enumerated therefore has no stated disposition: it is not admitted, because the allowed list is closed, but the payload is not refused either, so whether the host drops it silently and admits the rest is unspecified. That is a silent-admission hole in the one law this artifact exists to state. The hole is not hypothetical. File 01's same boundary table expressly forbids the component to 'set thresholds, waivers, verdict, or gate' and to 'narrow/widen domain or convert unknown to covered'. Measured in the artifact: 'threshold' 0, 'waiver' 0, 'narrow' 0, 'widen' 0, 'unknown' 0. Only 'verdict' made the forbidden list. So a payload that sets a threshold, sets a waiver, narrows or widens the Coverage domain, or converts unknown to covered is neither allowed nor forbidden, and the contract states no refusal for any of them — while the Coverage note addresses sufficiency alone.
blockers.whyBlocking: A refusal law with an unspecified region is not a law; it is a list. The attack prompt names silent fallback as a rejection class, and this is that defect in its precise form: the artifact's own closed allowed-list implies the right answer, but the operative rule does not state it, and three prohibitions that accepted architecture makes explicit are absent from the enumeration the rule depends on.
blockers.repair: Make the rule total by keying refusal to the allowed list: any component output outside {semanticFact, coverage} is refused, with the enumeration retained as named instances rather than as the trigger. Then add the missing instances from file 01's boundary table — thresholds, waivers, and Coverage domain narrowing/widening or unknown-to-covered conversion — so the enumeration and the architecture agree, and extend the Coverage note beyond sufficiency to the domain prohibitions.

coordinatorSummary: REJECT at 2 blockers and 3 SHOULD-FIX. Sixteen attacks run, six landed. Custody is intact: subject 237efad5 at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, HEAD never left 52ea851, file 08 at the dispatch pin 7585325d with a clean tree. Much of this artifact is strong. The row quoting is exact — source digest, table header and acceptance cell all reproduce byte-for-byte from live file 08 — the obligation decomposition reconstructs the cell with nothing left unassigned, every authority disclaimer is present and unhedged, and it invents nothing owned by DR-131, DR-117, DR-007 or §7.1. Four of the prompt's seven attack classes are refuted outright. What blocks is the relationship to architecture that already exists. DR-133's subject is the component-output boundary, and file 01 states that boundary in a table it expressly calls closed, at digest 40ab9a3e — the digest at which DR-201's re-review was ACCEPTED. File 01 lets a component RETURN candidate findings, typed faults and cancellation detail, declared requirements, capability negotiation input and candidate artifacts, reserving ADMISSION to the host. This artifact admits exactly two outputs and refuses payloads containing findings. It never cites file 01 — zero occurrences of file 01, 01-semantic or boundary — and never scopes itself to the preview — zero occurrences of preview — so it cannot be read on its face as a lawful role-scoped narrowing. Its own hostOwned list still carries admissionOfFindings with nothing left to admit. v1-slice §8 requires stopping and recording a design delta in exactly this situation. The second blocker is the mirror image: the refusal rule triggers on the eight-item forbidden enumeration rather than on absence from the two-item allowed list, so anything outside both has no stated disposition, and the enumeration omits three acts file 01 expressly forbids — setting thresholds, setting waivers, and narrowing or widening the Coverage domain or converting unknown to covered, all measured at zero occurrences. A refusal law with an unspecified region is a list, not a law. The three SHOULD-FIX are that findingLikeResult, the term carrying the anti-rename load, is undefined and untested against a corpus that has already recorded a rename defeating a checker; that the required 'typed non-success' names no existing v1.14 class and does not route the selection to DR-007, whose row holds that V2 cannot define the typed result or exit; and that five of eight declared prohibitions have a retained test class. All five findings are addressable in a v2 without restructuring: cite file 01, choose and record either a scoped narrowing or an alignment, make the refusal rule total by keying it to the allowed list, and close the definition and test gaps.
